title: Your next privacy breach might not leak any data at all

content_html:
For decades, protecting privacy has meant one thing: stop personal data from leaking out. Gartner thinks that idea is about to break.

By 2029, most privacy incidents will come not from leaked personal data but from what AI infers about people, the research firm predicted this week. The risk is no longer only the records a company holds. It is the conclusions a model can draw from scraps that look harmless.

From data exposure to insight exposure

Gartner analyst Bart Willemsen calls it a shift “from data exposure to insight exposure.” A model can now reconstruct deeply personal things, like a health condition or a behavioural pattern. It pulls them from data that looks anonymous, aggregated or harmless, and never has to breach a database to do it.

There is an irony in this. Companies are storing less personal data, pushed by regulation and cost. That is meant to reduce risk. But if an AI can infer the sensitive detail anyway, holding less data does little to protect the person it describes.

Attacks that leave no leaked record

These inference attacks are hard to catch. A normal breach leaves a trail: a stolen file, an exposed record, an alert that fires. An inferred conclusion leaves none of that.

“Inference attacks are particularly dangerous because they often evade conventional detection mechanisms,” Willemsen said. “Individuals can be exposed through AI-generated conclusions rather than leaked records, creating privacy risks that undermine data integrity and are difficult to detect, explain and mitigate.”

The threat also sits outside most privacy law, which largely governs personal data that companies collect, store and share. A guess a model makes is none of those things. It is a growing blind spot as everyday tools quietly record and analyse more of our lives.

What Gartner wants companies to change

Gartner’s advice to security chiefs is to govern what AI concludes, not just what it stores. It expects spending on data “integrity” protections to reach parity with data confidentiality by 2028, as firms respond to inaccurate, biased or unauthorised AI-generated profiles.

Its recommended fixes are practical. Bake privacy checks into how teams build AI systems. Adopt privacy-enhancing tools such as differential privacy and synthetic data. Minimise the data on hand. And keep a human in the loop to sign off before an AI acts on a sensitive inference.

That last point matters because the exposure can be quiet and accidental, not just malicious. TNW has covered how private AI chats ended up indexed by search engines, no breach required.

A prediction, not a certainty

The usual caveats apply. This is a Gartner forecast, and Gartner sells the research and the conference seats behind it. “Most privacy incidents” by a given year is the kind of claim that is easy to state and hard to prove.

But the underlying worry is real. Researchers have shown for years that models can re-identify people and guess private traits from public data. Regulators are only starting to catch up, with the EU’s AI Act still bedding in. Gartner’s point is simply that the industry has spent years guarding the wrong door.

content_html_zh:
几十年来，保护隐私意味着一件事：阻止个人数据泄露。 Gartner 认为这个想法即将被打破。

该研究公司本周预测，到 2029 年，大多数隐私事件将不是来自泄露的个人数据，而是来自人工智能对人的推断。 风险不再只是公司持有的记录。 这是模型从看似无害的碎片中得出的结论。

从数据暴露到洞察暴露

Gartner 分析师 Bart Willemsen 称之为“从数据暴露到洞察力暴露”的转变。 模型现在可以重建深度个人事物，例如健康状况或行为模式。 它从看似匿名、聚合或无害的数据中提取数据，而且无需破坏数据库即可完成此操作。

这其中有一个讽刺之处。 在监管和成本的推动下，公司存储的个人数据越来越少。 这是为了降低风险。 但如果人工智能无论如何都能推断出敏感细节，那么持有较少的数据对保护它所描述的人几乎没有帮助。

不留下任何泄露记录的攻击

这些推理攻击很难捕获。 正常的违规行为会留下痕迹：被盗的文件、暴露的记录、触发的警报。 推断的结论没有留下任何内容。

“推理攻击特别危险，因为它们经常逃避传统的检测机制，”威廉森说。 “个人可以通过人工智能生成的结论而不是泄露的记录而暴露，从而产生破坏数据完整性的隐私风险，并且难以检测、解释和缓解。”

这种威胁也不在大多数隐私法的范围内，该法主要管辖公司收集、存储和共享的个人数据。 模型所做的猜测都不是这些。 随着日常工具悄悄地记录和分析我们更多的生活，这是一个日益严重的盲点。

Gartner 希望企业改变什么

Gartner 对安全主管的建议是管理人工智能得出的结论，而不仅仅是它存储的内容。 随着企业对人工智能生成的不准确、有偏见或未经授权的配置文件做出反应，预计到 2028 年，数据“完整性”保护方面的支出将达到与数据机密性相当的水平。

它推荐的修复方法很实用。 将隐私检查纳入团队构建人工智能系统的方式中。 采用差异隐私和合成数据等隐私增强工具。 尽量减少手头的数据。 在人工智能根据敏感推理采取行动之前，让人类参与其中并签字同意。

最后一点很重要，因为曝光可能是悄悄的、偶然的，而不仅仅是恶意的。 TNW 报道了私人人工智能聊天如何最终被搜索引擎索引，无需违规。

预测，而非确定

通常的警告适用。 这是 Gartner 的预测，Gartner 出售其背后的研究和会议席位。 某一年“最多的隐私事件”是一种容易陈述但难以证明的说法。

但潜在的担忧是真实的。 研究人员多年来已经证明，模型可以重新识别人并从公共数据中猜测私人特征。 监管机构才刚刚开始迎头赶上，欧盟的人工智能法案仍在完善中。 Gartner 的观点很简单，就是该行业多年来一直把守着错误的大门。
